 Caleb Wilson will not return to Wednesday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Wilson, who was a game-time call for Wednesday due to a right hip injury, exited during the third quarter with an apparent right hand injury. Patrick Williams replaced Wilson at the time of the injury and could find himself back in the rotation if the rookie misses time. Wilson finished with 15 points, five rebounds, one steal and two three-pointers.

 Caleb Wilson (hip) is questionable to play against the Spurs on Wednesday. 
 Wilson has a chance to miss a game for the first time in his career. If that happens, one of either Patrick Williams or Noa Essengue will likely replace him in the starting lineup, though neither would be considered priority streaming options in that scenario. 
 Caleb Wilson 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 #8 
 Caleb Wilson amassed 18 points (7-of-18 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the 76ers. 
 This wasn’t Wilson’s most efficient game; he needed 18 shots to score 18 points. However, he has committed three turnovers or fewer in eight straight games, a far cry from the nine he committed in his debut against the Raptors. Despite shooting 40.6 percent from the field, Wilson is providing top-100 fantasy value, which aligns with his preseason ADP.

 Caleb Wilson recorded five points (2-of-12 FGs), five rebounds, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks. 
 After scoring at least 16 points in each of his first seven appearances, Wilson had his first bad game as a pro. The rookie forward shot 2-of-12 from the field, making just one of seven three-point attempts. Even worse for category-league managers was that the overall stat line was subpar. Wilson will look to bounce back on Sunday against the 76ers in another challenging matchup.

 Caleb Wilson led the Bulls with 24 points (9-of-17 FGs), seven rebounds, four assists, four steals and four three-pointers in a 126-107 loss to the 76ers on Monday. 
 Wilson continues to be the star of the show in Chicago, and it has worked out well in fantasy basketball. This was the first game he didn’t record at least one steal and one block, but he made up for it with a career high in steals. He has dished out exactly four assists and scored at least 20 points in three straight games, and he has scored fewer than 20 points in only two games. Plus, he has 13 triples over their last three games. The expectation was that he would be a fantasy stud, but his offensive production wasn’t supposed to be this good this quickly.

 Caleb Wilson accounted for 23 points (7-of-16 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal, two blocks and six three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Celtics. 
 Perimeter shooting was seen as a weakness of Wilson’s during the pre-draft process, and he entered Friday shooting 22.2 percent from beyond the arc. Against the Celtics, the rookie forward made six of his 11 attempts as part of a complete stat line. Wilson has been one of the most valuable rookies in fantasy basketball so far, and that shouldn’t change anytime soon.

 Caleb Wilson accounted for 20 points (7-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, two steals, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks. 
 Wilson has scored 20 or more points in three of his last four games and continues to improve. The Bulls’ rookie didn’t shoot as well as he can against the Knicks, but he still made an impact on both ends of the floor. The Bulls led by as much as 19 in the third quarter before the Knicks rallied to win. Wilson will be a fun player to watch develop in the years to come, and his fantasy value should only improve.

 Caleb Wilson recorded 17 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Celtics. 
 Monday’s matchup was tough for Wilson, as the Celtics rolled out a lineup led by Jayson Tatum and Paul George. However, the rookie forward finished Monday’s defeat 6-of-10 from two and managed to do a little bit of everything in his 32 minutes on the floor. The Bulls may be 1-3, but Wilson’s start to the season has been encouraging overall.

 Caleb Wilson recorded 30 points (10-of-24 FGs, 9-of-11 FTs), 14 rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Wizards. 
 After an inefficient debut on Wednesday, Wilson has been excellent in the Bulls’ last two games. He finished Saturday’s defeat with his first 30-point game, making some history in the process. Wilson’s 67 points are the second-most scored by a Bulls player in their first three NBA games. The record-holder: Michael Jordan, who scored 74 points in his first three games. Wilson and the Bulls play three games in Week 2, starting with the Celtics on Monday.

 RJ will have games where he will take a bunch of shots and miss a lot of them. The Raptors were without Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes in this one, so the Raptors needed the offense.  Immanuel Quickley scored 11 points (3-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, a steal, and a three in 98-93 loss to the Celtics. 
 IQ was returning from a hamstring injury and this was his first game back. On the season, IQ has been shooting 38.7% from the field which is just not good enough. He’s a career 42.4% field goal shooter which should show that there is room for him to bounce back, but it’s undoubtedly been a slow start efficiency wise.  Josh Hart (illness) finished Wednesday’s loss to the Cavaliers with six points (3-of-8 FGs), four rebounds and three assists.
 Hart returned to the Knicks lineup after a three-game absence, and he looked a bit rusty. His missed time and early foul trouble kept Hart to 26 minutes, and he recorded no defensive stats. Landry Shamet, who returned to the bench with Hart available, contributed 12 points, two rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in 29 minutes. A good chunk of Shamet’s minutes came at the expense of Mikal Bridges (two points, one rebound and two assists in 17 minutes), whose struggles continue.
